title: English Practice Exam 2024
description: English Practice Exam 2024 - 100 multiple choice questions. Ethiopian national exam preparation material.

questions.questionText: Although she had never visited the city before, she quickly found ___ apartment near ___ university where she had been admitted.
questions.explanation: "Apartment" begins with a vowel sound, so "an" is required. "University" begins with the consonant sound /juː/, so "a" is correct.

questions.questionText: The researcher bought ___ unusual instrument from ___ European manufacturer specializing in laboratory equipment.
questions.explanation: "Unusual" begins with a vowel sound, while "European" begins with /juː/, a consonant sound.

questions.questionText: After ___ long discussion, the committee reached ___ agreement that satisfied all the members.
questions.explanation: "Long discussion" is a nonspecific singular countable noun phrase, while "agreement" begins with a vowel sound.

questions.questionText: She hopes to become ___ engineer after completing ___ engineering degree at the university.
questions.explanation: Both "engineer" and "engineering" begin with vowel sounds, so "an" is used.

questions.questionText: ___ honesty is essential in academic research, but ___ honesty expected in this particular experiment was unusually strict.
questions.explanation: The first "honesty" is general and uncountable, while the second is made specific by "expected in this particular experiment."

questions.questionText: We saw ___ eagle near the river, and ___ bird remained in the same area for several minutes.
questions.explanation: "Eagle" begins with a vowel sound, and the second mention refers to the already identified bird.

questions.questionText: ___ water in this container is contaminated, but ___ water is essential for human survival.
questions.explanation: The first refers to specific water in the container; the second refers to water generally.

questions.questionText: ___ students who attended the seminar received ___ certificate at the end of the session.
questions.explanation: "Students" is a general plural noun, while "certificate" is a singular countable noun referring to one certificate per student.

questions.questionText: ___ students who were selected for the scholarship must submit ___ additional document.
questions.explanation: "The students" refers to a specific identified group, and "additional" begins with a vowel sound.

questions.questionText: He was appointed ___ director of the institution after serving as ___ senior researcher for five years.
questions.explanation: Job titles used after verbs such as "appointed" can take zero article when functioning as a title; "senior researcher" is an indefinite profession.

questions.questionText: She works as ___ accountant for ___ international organization based in Nairobi.
questions.explanation: Both "accountant" and "international" begin with vowel sounds.

questions.questionText: The conference was held at ___ university whose main campus overlooks ___ Indian Ocean.
questions.explanation: "University" begins with /juː/, so "a" is used. Oceans take "the."

questions.questionText: They traveled across ___ Sahara before reaching ___ Mediterranean coast.
questions.explanation: The Sahara is a desert name that takes "the," and the Mediterranean is a specific sea.

questions.questionText: Mount Everest is higher than ___ Alps, but climbing ___ individual mountain requires different equipment.
questions.explanation: Mountain ranges take "the," while "individual mountain" is a singular countable noun used nonspecifically.

questions.questionText: ___ Ethiopia is located in ___ Horn of Africa.
questions.explanation: Most country names take no article, while "the Horn of Africa" is a specific geographical region.

questions.questionText: The expedition crossed ___ Nile before entering ___ remote desert region.
questions.explanation: The Nile takes "the," while "a remote desert region" introduces a nonspecific singular countable noun.

questions.questionText: She lives near ___ Lake Victoria and often studies the wildlife around ___ lake.
questions.explanation: Individual lakes normally take no article. The second reference is specific and therefore takes "the."

questions.questionText: ___ United Kingdom consists of several countries, whereas ___ France is generally treated as a single country.
questions.explanation: The United Kingdom takes "the," while France normally takes no article.

questions.questionText: The plane flew over ___ Atlantic Ocean before reaching ___ European coast.
questions.explanation: Oceans take "the." "European" begins with the consonant sound /juː/, so "a" is used.

questions.questionText: After the accident, the injured man was taken to ___ hospital, while his brother went to ___ hospital to visit him.
questions.explanation: The first refers to the institution's main purpose of treatment; the second refers to a specific hospital building.

questions.questionText: The children go to ___ school by bus, but their parents went to ___ school to meet the principal.
questions.explanation: "Go to school" refers to its normal educational function; "the school" identifies a particular building.

questions.questionText: He stayed in ___ bed all morning because he had ___ severe headache.
questions.explanation: "In bed" is a fixed expression with zero article. "A severe headache" is a singular countable noun phrase.

questions.questionText: The researchers arrived at ___ work early because they had ___ important experiment to conduct.
questions.explanation: "At work" is a fixed expression. "Important" begins with a vowel sound, so "an" is required.

questions.questionText: We traveled to the conference ___ car rather than ___ bus because the equipment was too large.
questions.explanation: The fixed transport expressions are "by car" and "by bus."

questions.questionText: She speaks ___ English fluently, but she is studying ___ English used in nineteenth-century Ethiopia.
questions.explanation: English generally takes zero article, but the second phrase identifies a specific variety of English.

questions.questionText: ___ mathematics is difficult for some students, but ___ mathematics of this particular proof is exceptionally complex.
questions.explanation: The academic subject is general; the second refers to the specific mathematics involved in the proof.

questions.questionText: She studied ___ history at university, especially ___ history of the Ethiopian Empire.
questions.explanation: History as an academic subject takes zero article; the history of a specific entity is identified with "the."

questions.questionText: The athlete plays ___ football professionally but watched ___ football match from the stands yesterday.
questions.explanation: Sports generally take zero article; a specific match is a singular countable noun and takes "a."

questions.questionText: We had ___ breakfast at home, but ___ breakfast served at the hotel was much better.
questions.explanation: Meals generally take zero article; the second breakfast is specifically identified by "served at the hotel."

questions.questionText: ___ music can influence people's emotions, but ___ music played during the ceremony was particularly moving.
questions.explanation: Music in general takes zero article; the second refers to specific music.

questions.questionText: I need ___ pen. Could you lend me ___ pen you used during the examination?
questions.explanation: The first pen is unspecified; the second is identified by the relative clause.

questions.questionText: She bought ___ book yesterday. ___ book contains several chapters on modern physics.
questions.explanation: The first mention uses "a"; the second mention uses "the" because the book is now identified.

questions.questionText: A researcher found ___ solution to the problem, but ___ solution proved impossible to implement.
questions.explanation: The first solution is introduced as one possibility; the second refers to that identified solution.

questions.questionText: ___ first applicant arrived early, but ___ second applicant arrived only after the interview had begun.
questions.explanation: Ordinal expressions such as "the first" and "the second" normally take "the."

questions.questionText: She was ___ only student who completed ___ entire assignment before midnight.
questions.explanation: "The only" identifies a unique person, and "the entire assignment" refers to a specific complete assignment.

questions.questionText: This is ___ most difficult question in ___ examination.
questions.explanation: Superlatives take "the," and the examination is a specific identified examination.

questions.questionText: She chose ___ most reliable method available rather than ___ cheaper alternative.
questions.explanation: "The most reliable" is a superlative expression. "A cheaper alternative" introduces one nonspecific alternative.

questions.questionText: He was ___ first person to arrive and ___ last person to leave.
questions.explanation: Ordinal expressions "first" and "last" take "the."

questions.questionText: ___ next chapter explains the theory introduced in ___ previous chapter.
questions.explanation: "The next" and "the previous" identify particular chapters within the text.

questions.questionText: The lecturer gave us ___ useful piece of advice before ___ examination began.
questions.explanation: "Useful" begins with /juː/, so "a" is used. The examination is a specific known event.

questions.questionText: He waited for ___ hour outside ___ office before the manager arrived.
questions.explanation: "Hour" has a silent h and begins with a vowel sound. The office is a specific office identified by context.

questions.questionText: She is ___ honest researcher who always reports ___ results accurately.
questions.explanation: "Honest" begins with a vowel sound. "The results" refers to the specific results she reports.

questions.questionText: He is ___ European scientist who specializes in ___ study of climate change.
questions.explanation: "European" begins with /juː/, requiring "a." The specific field of study takes "the" in this context.

questions.questionText: She bought ___ one-way ticket because ___ train was scheduled to leave at noon.
questions.explanation: "One" begins with the consonant sound /w/, so "a" is used. The train is specific.

questions.questionText: The university hired ___ MBA graduate to lead ___ new business program.
questions.explanation: "MBA" is pronounced beginning with the vowel sound /em/, so "an" is required. The program is newly introduced and nonspecific.

questions.questionText: The company appointed ___ FBI agent to investigate ___ suspected fraud.
questions.explanation: "FBI" begins with the vowel sound /ef/. "A suspected fraud" introduces a nonspecific case.

questions.questionText: ___ information provided by the witness was insufficient to establish ___ clear connection between the two events.
questions.explanation: "Information" is uncountable but specific because it was provided by the witness. "A clear connection" is introduced as one possible connection.

questions.questionText: ___ information is often more valuable than ___ expensive equipment.
questions.explanation: Both uncountable nouns are used in a general sense, so no article is needed.

questions.questionText: ___ equipment in the laboratory must be checked before ___ experiment begins.
questions.explanation: The equipment is specifically identified by its location. The experiment is a specific upcoming experiment.

questions.questionText: The professor asked whether ___ research conducted last year supported ___ hypothesis proposed by the students.
questions.explanation: Both nouns refer to specific research and a specific hypothesis identified by additional information.

questions.questionText: Researchers need ___ patience when conducting ___ long-term study.
questions.explanation: "Patience" is an uncountable general noun. "A long-term study" introduces one study.

questions.questionText: ___ long-term study described in the report produced ___ unexpected result.
questions.explanation: The study is identified by "described in the report." "Unexpected" begins with a vowel sound.

questions.questionText: The researcher spent ___ hour examining ___ data collected during the previous experiment.
questions.explanation: "Hour" begins with a vowel sound. The data are specific because they were collected during a particular experiment.

questions.questionText: ___ data can be misleading if researchers ignore ___ context in which they were collected.
questions.explanation: "Data" is used generally, while "the context" is specifically identified by the relative clause.

questions.questionText: The researcher discovered ___ error in ___ original calculation.
questions.explanation: "Error" begins with a vowel sound, and the calculation is specific because it is the original one.

questions.questionText: She made ___ important discovery while examining ___ sample taken from the river.
questions.explanation: "Important" begins with a vowel sound. The sample is one of several possible samples, so "a" is appropriate.

questions.questionText: The scientist examined ___ sample taken from the river and compared it with ___ sample collected upstream.
questions.explanation: Both samples are specifically identified by their locations and have already been distinguished in the comparison.

questions.questionText: ___ second sample contained less contamination than ___ first.
questions.explanation: Ordinal references "the second" and "the first" identify particular items.

questions.questionText: The committee reached ___ unanimous decision after ___ hour of discussion.
questions.explanation: "Unanimous" begins with the consonant sound /juː/, so "a" is correct. "Hour" begins with a vowel sound.

questions.questionText: The manager described the proposal as ___ unique opportunity for ___ company.
questions.explanation: "Unique" begins with /juː/, so it takes "a." The company is specific in context.

questions.questionText: She received ___ European scholarship that allowed her to study at ___ university abroad.
questions.explanation: Both "European" and "university" begin with /juː/, a consonant sound.

questions.questionText: The professor gave ___ unusually difficult assignment to ___ class.
questions.explanation: "Unusually" begins with a vowel sound. "The class" identifies a particular group of students.

questions.questionText: ___ rich are not necessarily happier than ___ poor.
questions.explanation: "The + adjective" can refer to a whole social group, as in "the rich" and "the poor."

questions.questionText: Governments should provide greater support for ___ unemployed and ___ elderly.
questions.explanation: "The unemployed" and "the elderly" refer to groups of people sharing a characteristic.

questions.questionText: ___ lion is often used as an example of strength, while ___ lions in this reserve are being closely monitored.
questions.explanation: "The lion" can represent the species as a class. The second phrase refers specifically to lions in this reserve.

questions.questionText: ___ dogs are generally social animals, but ___ dogs living in this shelter require special care.
questions.explanation: The first plural noun is general; the second is specifically identified by the participial phrase.

questions.questionText: ___ education is essential for development, but ___ education provided by this institution is particularly rigorous.
questions.explanation: "Education" is general in the first phrase and specifically identified by the second phrase.

questions.questionText: The report discusses ___ importance of education in ___ developing countries.
questions.explanation: "The importance" is a specific concept identified by the following phrase, while "developing countries" is a general plural noun.

questions.questionText: ___ internet has transformed ___ way people communicate across national borders.
questions.explanation: "The internet" is treated as a unique identifiable system, and "the way" identifies a particular manner of communication.

questions.questionText: ___ Earth revolves around ___ Sun approximately once every year.
questions.explanation: The Earth and the Sun are unique celestial bodies in this context, so both take "the."

questions.questionText: ___ moon was visible above ___ mountains when the hikers reached the valley.
questions.explanation: The moon is treated as unique, and "the mountains" refers to the specific mountains in the scene.

questions.questionText: He climbed ___ mountain near the village, although he had previously climbed ___ Alps.
questions.explanation: An individual mountain introduced nonspecifically takes "a," while the mountain range takes "the."

questions.questionText: The students were asked to read ___ article about climate change before attending ___ lecture.
questions.explanation: "Article" begins with a vowel sound. The lecture is a specific lecture known from the context.

questions.questionText: I read ___ article yesterday. Today, I discussed ___ article with my professor.
questions.explanation: The first mention is "an article"; the second refers to that known article.

questions.questionText: The professor recommended ___ book that explains ___ theory in greater detail.
questions.explanation: The book is introduced as one book. The theory is a particular theory identified in context.

questions.questionText: The professor recommended ___ book on the table and ___ article published in a scientific journal.
questions.explanation: "The book" is specific because of "on the table." "Article" begins with a vowel sound and is introduced nonspecifically.

questions.questionText: She wants to become ___ doctor, but she has not yet chosen ___ medical school.
questions.explanation: Professions take a/an, and the medical school is not yet specifically identified.

questions.questionText: He hopes to attend ___ medical school near his home because ___ school offers a specialized program.
questions.explanation: The first school is one nonspecific school near his home; the second refers back to that identified school.

questions.questionText: She earns $10 ___ hour working as ___ assistant in a laboratory.
questions.explanation: The fixed rate expression is "an hour," and "assistant" begins with a vowel sound.

questions.questionText: The machine can process 500 samples ___ hour, making it ___ extremely efficient device.
questions.explanation: The rate expression uses "an hour," and "extremely" begins with a vowel sound.

questions.questionText: The train travels at approximately 100 kilometers ___ hour and reaches ___ capital before sunset.
questions.explanation: The fixed rate expression is "an hour," and the capital is a specific city identified by context.

questions.questionText: ___ number of applicants increased this year, but ___ number of available positions remained unchanged.
questions.explanation: "A number of" means several and takes an indefinite article; "the number of" refers to a specific total.

questions.questionText: ___ number of students applied for ___ scholarship offered by the university.
questions.explanation: "A number of students" means several students. The scholarship is specific because it is identified by the university's offer.

questions.questionText: ___ majority of the participants supported ___ proposal presented by the committee.
questions.explanation: "The majority" refers to a particular group, and the proposal is specifically identified by the following phrase.

questions.questionText: ___ majority of students prefer ___ online resources to printed materials.
questions.explanation: "A majority of" can mean a large portion without identifying a particular majority. "Online resources" is a general plural noun.

questions.questionText: ___ first chapter introduces ___ basic principles that are necessary for understanding the subject.
questions.explanation: "The first" is an ordinal expression, and the basic principles are specific principles necessary for the subject.

questions.questionText: The researcher arrived at ___ conclusion that required ___ completely different approach.
questions.explanation: "The conclusion" is a specific conclusion reached by the researcher. "A completely different approach" introduces one approach.

questions.questionText: After ___ investigation, the police identified ___ person responsible for the theft.
questions.explanation: "Investigation" begins with a vowel sound. The person is specific because the investigation identified that individual.

questions.questionText: After ___ investigation, the police discovered ___ unusual pattern in the financial records.
questions.explanation: Both "investigation" and "unusual" begin with vowel sounds.

questions.questionText: The investigators found ___ pattern in the records, and ___ pattern appeared in several other cases.
questions.explanation: The first mention introduces one pattern; the second refers to that already identified pattern.

questions.questionText: ___ evidence collected from the scene was insufficient to prove ___ defendant's guilt.
questions.explanation: The evidence is specific because it was collected from the scene. The defendant is a specific person in the case.

questions.questionText: ___ evidence is necessary before making ___ serious accusation.
questions.explanation: "Evidence" is uncountable and general. "A serious accusation" introduces one possible accusation.

questions.questionText: The committee needs ___ evidence before it can reach ___ final decision.
questions.explanation: "Evidence" is uncountable and used generally; "a final decision" introduces one eventual decision.

questions.questionText: ___ final decision will be announced after ___ committee completes its review.
questions.explanation: Both nouns refer to specific items identified by the context.

questions.questionText: The university has introduced ___ new policy requiring ___ students to carry identification cards.
questions.explanation: "A new policy" introduces one policy. "Students" is used generally as a plural group.

questions.questionText: ___ new policy introduced last month requires ___ student to carry identification.
questions.explanation: "The new policy" is specific because of "introduced last month." "Each student" refers to every individual in the group.

questions.questionText: ___ same problem occurred during ___ previous experiment.
questions.explanation: "The same" and "the previous" are identifying expressions that take "the."

questions.questionText: This method produces ___ same results as ___ method used in the earlier study.
questions.explanation: "The same" takes "the," and the second method is specific because it is identified by the earlier study.

questions.questionText: The researcher chose ___ least expensive option because ___ budget was limited.
questions.explanation: Superlatives take "the," and the budget is a specific budget belonging to the project.

questions.questionText: ___ last question on ___ examination was considerably harder than the others.
questions.explanation: "The last" is an identifying ordinal expression, and the examination is specific.
